strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime owns a named headless run session advance and persists checkpoint state for the next caller.
The run session advance writes bounded HeadlessRunSessionAdvanced evidence and session checkpoint files without raw prompts, provider responses, files, commands, paths, or environment values.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting persistent_structured_ledger and Rust-owned execution authority.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive drives an existing runtime-owned session checkpoint through repeated bounded session advances until a safe stop boundary or drive budget limit.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M17.1 headless.run.advance owns one session sequence, but callers still sequence repeated checkpoint-to-checkpoint advances and lost-response recovery externally.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External schedulers or wrappers would still own repeated long-running run-control orchestration outside the Rust runtime.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M16.1/M16.2 handled verification retry admission/execution and M17.1 added one session advance; M17.2 adds repeated runtime-owned drive from an existing checkpoint.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. A narrow headless.run.drive method is justified for drive-level replay state spanning multiple session advances; it is not a report or inspection RPC.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result is tied to an actual advance attempt and persisted checkpoint, not a standalone status/report/readiness surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Valid calls execute repeated existing continuation/task.run steps through session advances, persist drive checkpoints, and replay committed drives without duplicate execution.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can authorize a bounded runtime-owned drive from durable checkpoint state instead of sequencing one advance per checkpoint externally.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the core M17 progression from one checkpoint primitive to bounded drive-to-stop-boundary run control.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M17.2 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm actual bounded drive execution and replay-safe persistence, not a headless status wrapper.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M17.1 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm actual run session checkpoint persistence and replay-safe execution, not a headless status wrapper.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts explicit authorization, session_id, drive_id, expected_start_session_sequence, max_advances 1-3, and max_steps_per_advance 1-3
a valid drive requires an existing M17.1 session checkpoint and rejects missing or stale checkpoint state before task execution
a valid drive derives subsequent session sequences and executes repeated existing headless.run.advance/headless.continue_once/task.run steps
the drive stops at the first safe stop boundary or explicit drive budget limit
replaying the same drive_id returns the persisted result with replayed=true and no duplicate TaskRunning, HeadlessRunSessionAdvanced, or drive evidence
VSIX validators reject raw output/path/env/file/content fields and inconsistent bounded counts
existing headless.run.advance, headless.continue_once, and direct task.run behavior remain compatible
no scheduler, background worker, automatic apply, automatic recovery, provider expansion, shell/git/network/service expansion, VSIX policy, or raw data exposure is introduced
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M17.2 merge, assess M17 for closeout before planning any additional run-control phase.
